The controller

The screen is the upgrade you feel on flight one.

Most beginner drones make you clip your phone into the controller, drain its battery, and squint at notifications mid-flight. The RC PTD2 bundle skips all of that — the live view, telemetry and controls live on a built-in screen. It is the single most “this feels pro” moment on a drone at this price, which is why this page leads with the controller, not the camera.

01

No phone to clip in

Unfold, power on, fly. The screen is already there — no mount, no cable, no pairing dance before every flight.

02

900 nits, readable in direct sun

A 5.5-inch screen bright enough to frame a shot in full sunlight, where a phone display washes out.

03

Your phone stays your phone

No battery drain, and no calls or notifications interrupting you while the drone is in the air.

04

A longer link: 16 km

The PTD2 reaches up to 16 km of video transmission. The older PTD1 phone controller manages 10 km.

The camera

A 1/1.3-inch sensor. The step up you can see in low light.

The headline upgrade over the Atom 2 is the sensor — up from 1/2-inch to 1/1.3-inch, the same sensor class as DJI's Flip. This is not a toy sensor with a 4K label.

  • 50MP stills, JPEG + RAW — real files to edit, not just to post.
  • 4K/60fps HDR video — plus 2.7K vertical, shot ready for the feed.
  • P-Log colour — footage with room to grade, not baked-in contrast.
  • 3-axis mechanical gimbal — the horizon stays level while the drone moves.

Also on board: 4× digital zoom (2× at full 4K) and a dedicated night mode.

The honest section

Sold on its strengths. Straight about the rest.

What it does not have

No obstacle avoidance.

There are no sensing eyes on the Atom 3 — you fly it with your own eyes and the controller screen. This page says so plainly, in its own card, because a buyer who learns it here trusts the page more than one who learns it after buying.

Mitigation 01

Beginner Mode

Early flights are fenced to a 30-metre radius and height while you learn the sticks.

Mitigation 02

Return to Home

On low battery or signal loss, the Atom 3 flies itself back to its takeoff point.

The trade

Where the money went

Into the bigger sensor, the built-in screen and the battery — not into sensing hardware.

Fly open spaces first

Trees, power lines and crowds are not beginner territory on any drone without sensing.

Questions

Asked before every first flight.

Does it avoid obstacles?+

No. There is no obstacle-avoidance sensor on the Atom 3. Fly in open spaces, use Beginner Mode while you learn, and keep your eyes on the drone — the screen shows you the view, it does not steer around trees.

Why buy this instead of DJI's Lito 1 (Day 2)?+

The Lito 1 senses obstacles in every direction and costs less in the UK (£299) — but it has a smaller 1/2-inch sensor and no built-in screen controller. The Atom 3 trades sensing for a bigger sensor, a longer flight and a screen in your hands. That trade is the whole page.

How long does it really fly?+

Rated up to 40 minutes on the standard battery (50 on the higher-capacity battery) in lab conditions. Plan around roughly two-thirds of the rating in real flying, and remember the bigger battery can take it over 249g.

Can it shoot vertical for Reels and TikTok?+

Yes — 2.7K vertical shooting, made for social posting without re-editing the whole clip.

Can I buy it in the US or Nigeria?+

Availability varies: reviews note it is not officially sold through Potensic's US website, while it is widely listed across Europe. Check a retailer that ships to you before you promise a price — and in Nigeria, check NCAA requirements before you fly.

Skip the phone mount. Fly with a real screen.

The Atom 3, from £339.99 — or with the screen controller this page is about, from £499.
